messages:
maya: Quick follow-up on the canary/fallback architecture. I sketched a minimal upgrade pathway that avoids a huge refactor but still gives deterministic fallback. Want quick alignment before I write an RFC.
lin: +1, curious about what you mean by 'minimal' here.
sam: If it removes churn from the router, I'm in. We hit too many edge cases last quarter.
maya: Idea is a 3-phase approach: 1) local probe & warmup per instance, 2) edge traffic slice with an observer that only reads metrics, 3) progressive promotion with an enforced safety window and automatic fallback hooks.
noah: Can you paste the config sketch?
maya: Sure — rough YAML for a rollout policy: 
```
canary:
  variant: v2
  weight_steps: [1, 5, 20, 50]
  step_duration_sec: 300
  safety_signals:
    - p95_latency < 200ms
    - error_rate < 0.5%
  backoff_on_threshold_fail: true
  fallback: v1
```
jun: Nice. Where does the KV cache warmup live in that flow? We've seen cold-cache spikes skew p95.
maya: Good call — phase 1 (local probe) runs a scripted warmup that seeds KV cache for typical prefixes for that tenant. It's per-pod and must finish before the node marks itself healthy for canary traffic.
lin: How do we enforce that the router respects per-pod health vs just node health? Router currently only uses instance level liveness.
maya: Proposal: introduce a health-tier signal in the healthcheck API: `healthy: ready_for_canary | ready_for_prod` so router can select `ready_for_canary` when routing to canary slice. Minimal API change: extra enum on /health.
sam: That's neat and small. Any compatibility concerns with private deployments?
maya: Default behavior falls back to existing semantics (ready_for_prod == ready_for_canary). Private deploys can opt-in to finer-grained signals via a feature flag.
ops-bot: deploy-bot initiated canary for model-service v2 -> 1%
deploy-bot: Canary start - v2 @1% (id: canary-2456789012)
noah: Another big question: who owns rollback decision? Router, autoscaler, or a controller?
maya: Keep ownership in rollout controller: it evaluates the safety signals (metrics from tracing + blackbox probes) and invokes router toggle APIs. Controller also emits `fallback` events to audit log.
lin: What about split-brain between controller and manual ops changes? If someone manually flips routes, controller might fight it.
maya: Controller will set a short TTL on its route keys and refresh. Manual override writes a `manual_override` marker; controller will detect and pause automated changes and alert. That avoids conflicting dials.
sam: Thoughts on metric selection? p95 alone is noisy. Maybe a composite score.
maya: Agree — composite: weighted sum of p95, error_rate, and a quality signal (if available). Thresholds exposed in policy but default tuned conservatively.
noah: Can we make the safety check pluggable so we can add model-quality eval later?
maya: Yes pluggable function hooks. Minimal API: controller calls configured HTTP probe endpoint that returns JSON {status: ok|fail, score: 0.92}. Start simple, grow later.
jun: Any perf overhead from probes? If probes run too often they'll add noise.
maya: Keep probe cadence low in early steps (every 30s) and increase only after 20% traffic. Also sample only a small subset of tenants for quality probes.
lin: Sounds reasonable. Next: rollout telemetry contract. We need per-step snapshot exports for retrospective analysis.
maya: Plan: controller emits a StepEvent with metadata: step, weight, metrics_snapshot, action(take/rollback/pause). Those are pushed to telemetry pipeline with unique rollout id.
noah: We should also capture cache-warmup success state per-pod in the snapshot.
maya: Yup — include warmup_status and probe_latency histograms.
sam: One more ops concern: fast fallback to minimize error blast radius. What's target time-to-fallback?
maya: Target 2x detection window + propagation; with current infra that's ~45-60s for an emergency rollback. Controller can also trigger immediate all-traffic fallback if severe signal seen.
lin: OK. If this stays small API-wise (health-tier, route TTL, StepEvent), I can support the router changes.
maya: Great. I'll draft the RFC with those interface patches and a reference controller flow. Anyone want to coauthor?
jun: I'll help with probe design and warmup details.
noah: I'll take telemetry contract and rollout id format.
sam: I'll pair with lin on router TTL/override semantics.
maya: Perfect — thanks. I'll drop a short PR template and link the RFC here when done.
__notes: Do not include a title field per agents.md. This thread string is chronological and short-message style per Slack norms.
